accounting.rationale: J3/24-007 PDF 47, printed 33, lines 15-19 warns about compatibility effects of newly added intrinsic procedures. Existing main catalogues confirm the relevant mechanisms: doc/catalogues/external_statement_15_4_3_5.json for EXTERNAL statements, doc/catalogues/external_attribute_8_5_9.json for EXTERNAL attribute constraints, doc/catalogues/intrinsic_statement_15_4_3_7.json for INTRINSIC statements, and doc/catalogues/standard_generic_intrinsic_procedures_16_7.json for standard generic intrinsic names.
The document records that each Fortran International Standard since Fortran 77 defines more intrinsic procedures than its predecessor.

An older conforming program might be interpreted differently under a newer standard because an external procedure name can coincide with a new intrinsic name; this is a compatibility notice, not an extra diagnostic rule.

Specifying the EXTERNAL attribute is identified as the exception to the compatibility risk; concrete EXTERNAL statement/attribute coverage exists in doc/catalogues/external_statement_15_4_3_5.json and doc/catalogues/external_attribute_8_5_9.json.
